skill.name: sql-to-osc
skill.description: Convert Flyway SQL migration scripts into Online Schema Change text files using documented project formatting rules.
skill.summary: Converts Flyway ALTER TABLE and CREATE INDEX migrations into OSC text format.
skill.author: DennisLiuCk

content.user_title: Convert SQL Migrations to OSC Format
content.value_statement: Database teams often need Flyway migrations rewritten for Online Schema Change workflows. This skill converts ALTER TABLE and CREATE INDEX statements into tab-separated OSC lines.
actual_capabilities: Reads Flyway SQL migration content from the documented migration path.
Extracts database names, table names, and schema change operations.
Converts USE and ALTER TABLE wrappers into OSC columns.
Rewrites CREATE INDEX statements as ADD INDEX operations.
Formats OSC output with tabs, comma-joined operations, LF endings, and semicolons.
Provides a conversion summary with source file, output file, tables, and operation counts.
limitations: It documents conversion rules and does not include an executable parser.
It is focused on Flyway-style SQL and a project-specific OSC text format.
Complex SQL may require manual review before database deployment.
It does not validate generated OSC against a live database.

use_cases.title: Prepare OSC Migration Files
use_cases.description: Convert a Flyway migration into the expected OSC text file before release.

use_cases.title: Review Schema Change Output
use_cases.description: Check that table names, column changes, and index operations match the source SQL.

use_cases.title: Summarize Release Changes
use_cases.description: Create a concise summary of affected tables and operation counts for deployment notes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion for one Flyway file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Flyway migration to OSC format. Preserve the database, table, operations, separators, and final semicolon.

prompt_templates.title: Check Existing OSC Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate a generated OSC line against source SQL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this OSC output with the source migration. Identify missing operations, wrong table names, formatting issues, and type casing issues.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Multiple Statements
prompt_templates.scenario: Handle a migration with several table operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these migration statements into OSC rows. Group operations by database and table, and provide a conversion summary.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Migration Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Flyway migrations for OSC conversion. Produce OSC-ready output, flag ambiguous SQL, and summarize tables and operation counts.

output_examples.input: A Flyway file that selects one database, alters one table, and adds one index.
output_examples.output: A single OSC row with the database, table, normalized column change, and index addition.

output_examples.input: A migration that contains several ALTER TABLE operations for the same table.
output_examples.output: One OSC row with all operations joined in order and formatted with tab-separated columns.

output_examples.input: A release review request with source migration names and expected output date.
output: OSC-ready output description for each affected table.
A conversion summary with source files, output file name, tables, and operation counts.
A short list of SQL statements that need manual review.

best_practices: Review generated OSC lines with a database owner before release.
Keep source migration file names and output dates aligned with release plans.
Validate table names, data types, and index names against the target schema.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy converted OSC output without reviewing the generated file.
Do not use this skill for unrelated SQL dialect rewrites.
Do not assume complex multi-table migrations are safe without manual checks.

faq.question: What does this skill convert?
faq.answer: It converts Flyway SQL migration content into the documented Online Schema Change text format.

faq.question: Does it run database migrations?
faq.answer: No. It guides conversion and formatting. It does not execute SQL or connect to a database.

faq.question: Which SQL statements are covered?
faq.answer: The documented rules cover USE, ALTER TABLE, NULL handling, CREATE INDEX, and data type casing.

faq.question: Can it handle multiple operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can combine operations for the same table using comma-separated OSC operations.

faq.question: What output path does it use?
faq.answer: The skill documents output under src/main/resources/db/osc with a dated osc file name.

faq.question: Should the output be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review generated OSC output before deployment, especially for complex or high-risk schema changes.
